subject: general
question: Which state’s Gogabeel Lake has been recently designated as a Ramsar site, increasing India’s total to 94 wetlands of international importance?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Bihar’s Gogabeel Lake has been designated as a Ramsar site, raising India’s tally of wetlands of international importance to 94.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gogabeel Lake, located in Katihar district, is Bihar’s first community-managed oxbow lake situated between the Ganga and Mahananda rivers.**
 
• **With this addition, Bihar now has six Ramsar sites, ranking third after Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh.**
 
• **India remains the top country in Asia and third globally (after the UK and Mexico) with 94 Ramsar sites.**
 
• Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav announced the inclusion, noting that India added 67 sites in the last 11 years covering 13,60,805 hectar**es.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ramsar Convention**__

 __
 
• Adopted in 1971 in Ramsar, Iran, to conserve and ensure the wise use of wetlands.
 
• India is among the 172 member countries under this global treaty.
 
• Globally, there are 2,546 Ramsar sites covering critical wetland ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Gogabeel Lake**__
 __
 
• Type: Oxbow lake formed by the meandering of rivers.
 
• Location: Katihar district, Bihar, between the Ganga and Mahananda rivers.
 
• Significance: Serves as a key floodplain and biodiversity hotspot managed by local communities.
 
 
 
• **India’s Ramsar Site Rankings**__
 
 
• 1st in Asia with 96 sites.
 
• 3rd in the world after the United Kingdom (176) and Mexico (144).
 
• Recent additions include Gokul Jalashay (Buxar) and Udaipur Jheel (West Champaran), both in Bihar.
